summary: Cache-side memory delivery limits the kernel, rather than DRAM bandwidth or compute throughput.
reasoning: Memory SOL is 71.35% versus 38.7% compute throughput. L2 throughput reaches 75.21%, while DRAM throughput is only 16.32% and L2 hit rate is 95.62%, indicating predominantly cache-served traffic. Long-scoreboard stalls of 61.98% show substantial waiting on memory dependencies.

root_causes.cause: Low useful-byte utilization increases memory transaction pressure on the cache hierarchy.

evidence.interpretation: Global loads use only half the bytes per sector on average.
L2 is substantially busier than DRAM, consistent with cache-side transaction pressure.

fixes.fix: Profile A and B loads separately, then tune their tile layouts so neighboring lanes access contiguous elements along the actual unit-stride dimension.
fixes.rationale: Improving sector utilization reduces transactions required to deliver each operand tile.

root_causes.cause: Operand-load latency is insufficiently hidden by the available resident warps and pipeline overlap.

evidence.interpretation: Warps frequently wait for dependencies associated with L1/global-memory operations.
Moderate achieved occupancy limits the pool of warps available to cover memory latency.
Shared-memory allocation imposes a tighter block-residency limit than registers, whose limit is nine blocks.

fixes.fix: Expand autotuning across pipeline stages and tile sizes, selecting the configuration that improves load/compute overlap without sacrificing shared-memory-limited residency.
fixes.rationale: Balancing buffering against occupancy can reduce exposed load latency; increasing stages alone may worsen residency.
